"Fractions that contain multiple terms in the numerator and a single term in the denominator can be split into separate terms.

For example, 

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {x + 2} {3} &= \
		\dfrac x 3 + \dfrac 2 3
	}
$$

and

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {3a - 4b + 1} {5} &= \
		\dfrac {3a} 5 - \dfrac {4b} 5 + \dfrac 1 5.
	}
$$

Often, we're able to simplify the fractions in the individual terms, as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {10x + 9} {2} &= \
		\dfrac {10x} {2} + \dfrac 9 2 &= \
		\dfrac {10} {2} \cdot x + \dfrac 9 2 &= \	
		5 \cdot x + \dfrac 9 2 &= \
		5x + \dfrac 9 2 
	}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186064444 :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

		\dfrac x 3 + \dfrac 2 3
	}
$$

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {3a - 4b + 1} {5} &= \
		\dfrac {3a} 5 - \dfrac {4b} 5 + \dfrac 1 5.
	}
$$

$$

		\dfrac {10} {2} \cdot x + \dfrac 9 2 &= \	
		5 \cdot x + \dfrac 9 2 &= \
